newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Britain says supports U.S. missile attack on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Britain says supports U.S. missile attack on Iraq.

text.p: Britain strongly supports U.S. cruise missile attacks launched on Tuesday against targets in Iraq, British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said.
"We strongly support the action that has been taken by the U.S. against Iraq," Rifkind told a news conference in the Mongolian capital of Ulan Bator, where he is on an official visit.
The U.S. military on Tuesday launched cruise missile strikes against air defence targets in Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks against Kurdish groups, the Pentagon said.
Western allies had also extended the no-fly zone in southern Iraq closer to Baghdad to give allied forces more control over Iraqi air space.
"The extension of the no-fly zone and the other action taken has been a necessary consequence of the new aggression by (Iraqi leader) Saddam Hussein," Rifkind said.
He said Britain had discussed the strikes with the United States over the last two or three days and vowed further military action by Baghdad would be met with similar action.
"Saddam Hussein must learn in a hard way that every time he commits aggression, he loses more than he gains," Rifkind said.
"Any future aggression would inevitably invite a similar response," he said. "We know from the past that the man cannot be trusted."

The international community had a responsibility to punish Saddam for sending troops into Kurdish safe havens and to prevent him from stepping up military campaigns against the ethnic minority, Rifkind said.
"He sends 40,000 troops and hundreds of tanks and artillery against the Kurdish people in the town of Arbil," Rifkind said.
"If this action had been ignored by the international community, there would have been further aggression against the remainder of the Kurdish part of the country," he said.
